ayat.text: رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي

And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then offer what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal has reached its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head, making shaving necessary, must offer a ransom of fasting three days, or charity, or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever performs Umrah during the Hajj months, followed by Hajj offers what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find or afford such an animal, then a fast of three days during Hajj and of seven when you have returned home. Those are ten complete days. This is for those whose family is not in the area of Al-Masjid Al-Haram. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty.

Hajj is during well-known months. So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein, by entering the state of Ihram, there is to be from him no sexual relations and no disobedience and no disputing during Hajj. And whatever good you do, Allah knows it. And take provisions. But indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah. And fear me, O you of understanding.
فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ
وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ
الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ فَمَنْ فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ الْحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي الْحَجِّ

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Pilgrimage, Chapter: Recommendation of Stoning Jamrat al-Aqaba on a Mount, Hadith 1297
hadith.text: Jabir reported: I saw Rasulullah flinging pebbles while riding his camel on the day of Nahr, saying: Learn your rituals from me, for I do not know whether I would be performing Hajj after this Hajj of mine

hadith.expanded_reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Rites (Kitab al-Manasik), Chapter: Standing at Arafat, Hadith 1919
hadith.text: Yazid bin Shaiban said: We were standing in Arafat in a place far from the place of standing... Ibn Mirba' al-Ansari came and said: I am the messenger of Rasulullah... Stay where you are for it is a place of ritual, for you are following the legacy of your father Ibrahim

hadith.expanded_reference: Sunan Ibn Majah, Book of Rites (Kitab al-Manasik), Chapter: The Hajj of the Messenger of Allah, Hadith 2890
hadith.text: Rasulullah performed Hajj on an old saddle, wearing a cloak that was worth only four dirhams or less. Then he said: Allahumma hijjatun la riya'a fiha wala sum'ah — O Allah, a Hajj in which there is no showing off nor reputation sought

hadith.expanded_reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Rites (Kitab al-Manasik), Chapter: The Muhrim Who Breaks a Bone or Becomes Lame, Hadith 1862
hadith.text: Rasulullah said: If anyone breaks a bone or leg or becomes lame, he has come out of ihram and must perform Hajj the following year

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih Muslim, Book of Sacrifices, Chapter: The Age of Sacrificial Animals, Hadith 1963
hadith.text: Rasulullah said: Sacrifice only a grown-up animal unless it is difficult for you, in which case sacrifice a ram of more than six months of age

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Conditions, Chapter: Conditions in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, Hadith 2731
hadith.text: When Rasulullah made a peace deal with Quraysh... Um Salamah gave advice: Go out and do not say a word to anyone until you sacrifice your camel and call your barber to shave your head. When he did that, the Sahaba got up and offered their sacrifices

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Penalty for Hunting, Chapter: The One Who is Prevented on the Way to Hajj, Hadith 1806
hadith.text: Abdullah bin Umar set out for Makkah intending to perform Umrah during the time of fitnah... and said: If I should be prevented from reaching the Kaaba, I would do the same as Rasulullah did in the year of Hudaybiyyah

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj, Chapter: Matting the Hair Upon Entering Ihram, Hadith 1560
hadith.text: Hafsa said: Ya Rasulullah, why have the people finished their Ihram after performing Umrah but you have not? He replied: I have matted my hair and garlanded my hady, so I will not finish my Ihram till I have slaughtered my animal

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj, Chapter: Hajj at-Tamattu', Hadith 1571
hadith.text: Imran bin Husayn said: The verse of Tamattu' was revealed in Allah's Book, so we performed it with Rasulullah, and nothing was revealed in the Quran to make it illegal nor did Rasulullah prohibit it till he died

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj, Chapter: The One Who Inquires on the Day of Nahr While Standing on His Mount, Hadith 1736
hadith.text: Rasulullah stopped near Jamarat at Mina... A man said: I forgot and got my head shaved before slaughtering. He said: There is no harm, go and slaughter now... Whenever he was asked about anything performed before or after, his reply was: Do it now, there is no harm

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Penalty for Hunting, Chapter: The Verse: A Ransom of Fasting or Charity or Sacrifice, Hadith 1814
hadith.text: Ka'b bin Ujrah reported that Rasulullah said to him regarding his head lice: Have your head shaved, then either fast three days, or feed six poor persons, or slaughter one sheep as a sacrifice

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Fasting, Chapter: Fasting on the Days of Tashreeq, Hadith 1997
hadith.text: Aisha and Ibn Umar said: Nobody was allowed to fast on the days of Tashreeq except those who could not afford the sacrificial animal

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Fasting, Chapter: Fasting on the Days of Tashreeq, Hadith 1998
hadith.text: Ibn Umar said: During the Farewell Hajj, Rasulullah performed Umrah and Hajj and drove a hady... Whoever has driven the sacrificial animal should not finish their Ihram till he completes his Hajj, and whoever has not should do Tawaf, Sa'ee, cut hair, and finish Ihram

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj, Chapter: The Virtue of Hajj Mabroor, Hadith 1521
hadith.text: Whoever performs Hajj to this House and does not commit any obscenity nor any sin will come out as sinless as a newborn child

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Umrah, Chapter: The Obligation of Umrah and Its Virtue, Hadith 1773
hadith.text: The reward of Hajj Mabroor is nothing except Jannah

hadith.expanded_reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi, Chapters on Righteousness and Maintaining Good Relations, Chapter: What Has Been Related About Doing Good, Hadith 1956
hadith.text: Your smile for your brother is charity, commanding good and forbidding evil is charity, giving directions to a person who is lost is charity, guiding a man with bad sight is charity, and removing a stone, thorn, or bone from the path is charity

dua.text: اللَّهُمَّ حِجَّةٌ لَا رِيَاءَ فِيهَا وَلَا سُمْعَةَ
سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ

topics.name: Prophetic Authority and Ritual Adherence (Manasik)
topics.description: The command of Rasulullah to learn pilgrimage rites directly from his practice without human innovation.

topics.name: Sincerity and Exclusivity of Devotion (Ikhlas)
topics.description: Undertaking pilgrimage solely for the pleasure of Allah, completely free of ostentation, pride, or worldly gain.

topics.name: Jurisprudence of Ihsar (Impediments to Pilgrimage)
topics.description: Rules governing pilgrims prevented from completing Hajj or Umrah due to sickness, injury, or hostility.

topics.name: Sacrificial Animals and Fidya for Violations (Hady & Kaffarah)
topics.description: Compensatory ransoms of fasting, charity, or sacrifice for shaving or committing unavoidable Ihram infractions.

topics.name: Pilgrimage Modalities and Fasting Expiation (Tamattu' & Siyam)
topics.description: The legitimacy of Hajj Tamattu' and the substitution of ten fasts when sacrificial livestock cannot be procured.

topics.name: Etiquettes and Prohibitions of Pilgrimage (Ijtinab ar-Rafath wal-Fusuq)
topics.description: Strict prohibition of obscenity, sinful misconduct, and contentious disputes throughout the sacred journey.

topics.name: Spiritual Provision and Taqwa (Zad al-Akhirah)
topics.description: Cultivating personal worship, social beneficence, and the ultimate spiritual provision of God-consciousness.
